clauses.scope_note: CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 Section 8(a): applies to uses of Licensed Material that could lawfully be made without permission under the Public License; it does not grant permission where other law requires it.
clauses.condition_explanation: use_lawfully_possible_without_license_permission means the use is lawful without permission under this Public License. This preserves applicable exceptions and limitations; see the definition of Exceptions and Limitations.

coverage_notes: The chunk does not include external documents or incorporated terms needed to determine whether a particular use is lawful without permission.
Section 8(b) concerns reformation and severability, and Section 8(c) concerns waiver and consent; these are legal-effect provisions rather than activity constraints on the licensee.
The trademark restriction in the post-license notice applies to Creative Commons trademarks, not the licensed material, and the notice expressly states it is not part of the public licenses.

paragraph_audit.reason: Addresses whether the Licensor is bound by additional terms communicated by the licensee; it does not impose an activity constraint on the licensee.
Specifies the legal relationship of other agreements to the Public License, not a behavioral duty or activity permission.
Preserves uses of Licensed Material that can lawfully be made without permission under the Public License.
Provides for reformation or severance of unenforceable provisions; this is a legal-effect mechanism, not an activity constraint.
Addresses waiver and consent by the Licensor as a matter of legal effect; it does not specify a licensee activity constraint.
Preserves privileges and immunities; it does not impose an activity constraint.

The Creative Commons trademark restriction concerns use of Creative Commons marks, not a licensed-material activity constraint; the paragraph expressly says it does not form part of the public licenses.
